findings.title: Deauthentication / disassociation flood
findings.detail: 18 deauth-class frames from 04:42:1a:19:88:f8 inside a 5-second window -- the signature of a forced disconnect, used either as denial of service or to make a client reconnect so its four-way handshake can be captured
evidence: 29 frames total, peak 18 within 5 s starting at t+22.03 s
reason codes seen: 7 (class 3 frame received from nonassociated STA)
0/29 frames were cryptographically protected
none were protected, so every one of them is forgeable by any device in range
findings.benign_explanation: an access point rebooting, shedding clients under load, or steering a client to another band also emits deauths, though rarely this many this fast from one address

findings.title: Possible association disruption: conflicting AP responses
findings.detail: 3 connection attempts by 4c:03:4f:e4:ef:71 to AP 04:42:1a:19:88:f8 received an unprotected disconnect and then a successful association response from the same claimed AP. This inconsistent state can indicate spoofed pre-key disconnects, including on PMF-required networks
evidence: association request frame 1570, unprotected disconnect frame 1571 (reason 6), followed by successful association response within 1 s
association request frame 1901, unprotected disconnect frame 1902 (reason 6), followed by successful association response within 1 s
association request frame 1923, unprotected disconnect frame 1924 (reason 6), followed by successful association response within 1 s
findings.benign_explanation: capture reordering, stale retransmissions, or an AP firmware/state mismatch may also produce conflicting responses; this is a suspected disruption, not proof

findings.title: Unprotected deauth on an MFP-required network
findings.detail: "testnetworkRPT88" (04:42:1a:19:88:f8) requires management frame protection. Established protected associations should reject forged unprotected disconnects, but frames sent before key installation can still disrupt connection setup; this capture alone does not establish whether the frames were effective
evidence: RSN capabilities: MFP required

findings.title: Handshake metadata observed
findings.detail: AP 04:42:1a:19:88:f8 ("testnetworkRPT88"): handshake material was captured, but its presence alone does not establish offline password-guessing exposure. SAE, enterprise and OWE key establishment differ from PSK; mixed or unknown AKMs require confirmation of the authentication method used by this station
